data.body_html:
Planning a boat rental from Marbella in 2028? You’ve likely heard of Sotogrande, Cabopino, and Estepona – three popular destinations along the Costa del Sol. But which one suits your day on the water best? This guide compares distances, costs, and the best boats for each, so you can book with confidence. All our charters depart from Puerto Banús, the heart of Marbella’s luxury marina scene.

Sotogrande: The Luxury Marina Escape

Sotogrande is 35 km south of Puerto Banús – about 30 minutes by car or 1.5–2 hours by boat. It’s known for its exclusive marina, golf courses, and polo fields. For a full-day charter (8 hours), the Tier A Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 at €2,299 all-inclusive gives you time to cruise down, enjoy lunch at a waterfront restaurant, and return. If you’re short on time, the Tier B Mangusta 80 (€4,719/4h) includes a free jet ski for extra fun along the way.

Cabopino: Quick and Laid-Back

Cabopino is only 7 km east of Puerto Banús – a 10-minute drive or 20–30 minutes by boat. Its small marina and sandy beach with chiringuitos make it ideal for a half-day trip. The Dubhe (8m) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m) are perfect for up to 5 people (pricing on request), while the Fairline Targa 12m handles groups of 10. Anchor off the beach for a swim, then grab tapas at the beach bar. A 4-hour charter is plenty.

Estepona: Old Town Charm and Modern Marina

Estepona lies 15 km west of Puerto Banús – 15 minutes by car, 30–45 minutes by boat. The marina is modern, and the old town is a short walk away with flower-lined streets and authentic tapas. The coastline passes Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés, two beautiful coves for swimming. A 6-hour charter on the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax, pricing on request) gives you a comfortable day out. All charters include skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and 21% VAT.
